skills.name: Economic impacts of road and rail transport

note.text: Reliable transport can connect producers to customers, reduce some distribution costs, widen access to services and support employment. Effects depend on prices, service availability and who can use the link. Construction may also displace activities, divide habitats or increase pollution. More infrastructure alone does not prove a net benefit for every community.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain a transport benefit and cost without assuming equal outcomes. Builds on: road and rail development. Leads to: air and water transport decisions.

sections.heading: Explain the geography

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented market record, delivery cost for the same load falls from CFA {12000} to CFA {9000}. The saving is CFA {12000-9000}. This is a cost comparison for an identical shipment, not proof that every retail price falls by the same amount. Market competition, other costs and household access affect the outcome.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State the causal chain from the transport change to the effect. Compare equivalent loads and periods. Subtract the new cost from the old for the saving, and seek evidence about distribution of benefits and environmental costs.
